title: A Lipschitz map whose a.e. derivative is continuous has that derivative everywhere
statement: Let n, l >= 0, f : R^n -> R^l, g : R^n -> L(R^n, R^l), c in R^n, r real and K >= 0. If f is K-Lipschitz on the open ball B^o_r(c), g is continuous on B^o_r(c), and for Lebesgue-almost every x in B^o_r(c) the map f has Frechet derivative g(x) at x, then f has Frechet derivative g(x) at every x in B^o_r(c).
lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (g : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (c : Rn n) (r : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzOnWith K f (ball c r) → ContinuousOn g (ball c r) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), x ∈ ball c r → HasFDerivAt f (g x) x) → ∀ x ∈ ball c r, HasFDerivAt f (g x) x
